note: Order of the guided run (/gramatica/percurso) and of every topic list sorted by level (src/lib/lehrplan.js). This is a teaching decision, not a derived sort: within a level, what later topics build on comes first. The file keeps the old topic ids (German slugs); docs/content-plan.md §3 says which Portuguese topic each id holds. Portuguese order (2026-11-13, grammar-structure run): A1 starts with the subject pronouns (tu / você / o senhor), then gender, the articles with their contractions (do, no, ao, pelo) and plurals, then ser and estar and adjective agreement (which need gender), numbers, the present (regular, key irregular, vowel-change), questions, há/estar, and the small everyday structures; A2 starts with reflexives (the first enclisis), frequency and the two verb phrases that need no new forms (ir + infinitive, estar a + infinitive), then the three past forms (perfeito, irregular perfeito, imperfeito), verb + infinitive, the object and indirect-object pronouns with their enclisis, polite requests (imperfeito), comparison, place, quantity and negation; B1 opens with the perfeito composto against the perfeito simples, then perfeito vs imperfeito, the mais-que-perfeito composto and the participles, then the future and conditional, the imperative as the door to the subjunctive (its negative forms are subjunctive forms), the present subjunctive, the futuro do conjuntivo with its time clauses and real conditions, then relative clauses, indirect questions and the clitic-placement rules in one place (they need que, não and the subjunctive), and finally por/para, verbs + prepositions and the refinements; B2 starts with the imperfeito do conjuntivo and unreal conditions, because the following subjunctive topics use them, then the personal infinitive, and keeps reported speech until the conditional and the imperfect subjunctive are known; C1 starts with the sequence of tenses (mais-que-perfeito do conjuntivo), then the clause types, then mesoclisis and the simple mais-que-perfeito (reading forms), and ends with formal style. Only topics listed here are part of the run (core). Topics left out are extra practice (reference and word-formation topics: wortarten, wortbildung-nomen): they keep their page and their place in the index, but they do not lengthen the run. Each topic must be listed under its own `level`. Drafts ("status": "entwurf") only count once they are reviewed. An entry "id:A2" would be the A2 part of a topic that teaches two levels on one page (exercise titles "A2: …"); no Portuguese topic does this at the moment. `akkusativ` has its own page (/pronomes-complemento) and is named for the sorted lists, not as a run station. Keep GRAMMATIK_ORDER in src/lib/grammatikOrder.js in step.
